narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The word 'dhamal' or 'dhamail' is found in Bengali poetry from the 14th century onwards, including works by Chandidas of Birbhum and poets from Chittagong in the 16th and 17th centuries.
Folk composers Radharaman Dutta and Arkum Shah are credited with introducing the dhamail dance tradition to Sylhet.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Dhamail is performed mainly by women during marriages and auspicious events.
The dance symbolizes the spiritual union of the newlywed couple, reflecting the devotional love of Radha and Krishna.
The escalating tempo and removal of dancers represent intensifying devotion and unity of souls.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Male musicians accompany the dance playing mirdanga drums and kartals (hand cymbals), among other instruments.
The rhythm accelerates progressively, driving the dance's increasing tempo and intensity.
Listen for the mirdanga, kartals, other percussion instruments.

The music features rhythmic drum beats from the mirdanga and sharp clashing sounds from the kartals, supporting a lead vocalist whose devotional songs are echoed by a chorus of women, building in tempo and intensity.
